title: Tenant-aware metric sampling and synthetic latency anchors for inference KPIs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: High-cardinality tenant labels and per-request inference metadata are driving Prometheus ingest costs and query tail latency. We need a pipeline-level approach that preserves SLO signal while reducing storage and cardinality explosion for multi-tenant hosted and dedicated deployments.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware sampling layer and introduce 'synthetic latency anchors' that ensure each tenant retains representative latency samples across percentiles (p50/p95/p99) without storing full per-request series. This reduces cardinality, keeps SLO observability, and allows consistent SLO computation in the downstream analytics layer.

Scope: collector-side and collector-central (OTel) processors, downstream Prometheus remote-write pipeline hooks, and dashboard changes. Does NOT include quota enforcement or billing model changes in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A configurable sampler can be applied per-tenant with default sampling rates and override rules (by label and route).
Synthetic latency anchors emit one anchored datapoint per tenant per minute for p50/p95/p99 buckets and are tagged with stable anchor labels that do not increase cardinality.
End-to-end test shows >=3x reduction in series cardinality for high-cardinality tenants while maintaining <5% deviation in computed p95 SLO for simulated workloads.
Integration tests and a canary in staging for 2 weeks with rollback plan and metrics to detect regressions.
Dashboard widgets updated to surface sampling rates and synthetic-anchor coverage per tenant.
Documentation and runbook for enabling per-tenant sampling and anchor tuning published.
technical_design:
High level: 1) Add Otel collector processor 'tenant_sampler' that implements deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by tenant_id + route signature. 2) Implement an 'anchor_generator' downstream processor that consumes sampled and unsampled latency streams and emits synthetic anchor series: stable label set (tenant_id, synthetic_anchor=true, bucket=p50/p95/p99) with latency values computed from a short time-window aggregator. 3) At the remote-write gateway (Prometheus bridge), mark sampled series with a sample_rate label and apply aggregation rules that collapse high-cardinality labels into tenant-level rollups. 4) Provide configuration: per-tenant policy store (ConfigMap / Consul / DS API) with default sample_rate and anchor windows.

Implementation notes: Use Otel processor framework to keep changes deployable in both hosted collector and dedicated sidecars. Anchor generator should be time-windowed and resilient to out-of-order data; use tumbling windows of 1m with max-lateness 15s. Store per-tenant reservoirs in memory with LRU eviction for cold tenants. Metrics emitted by processors: sampler.accepted, sampler.dropped, anchor.emitted, reservoir.size.

Backward compatibility: When sampling is disabled, anchors must not be emitted. Existing dashboards must be able to compute SLO from either raw latency series or anchors depending on tenant config.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind telemetry.sampling.enable; default off for all tenants.
Stage 1: Deploy processors to staging Otel collector and run synthetic workload to validate anchor correctness.
Stage 2: Canary 5% of tenants in canary cluster for 2 weeks, monitor sampler.* and anchor.* metrics plus SLO drift dashboard.
Stage 3: Ramp canary tenants to 50% if SLO drift <5% and no backend errors; then 100% in dedicated regions.
Rollback: telemetry.sampling.enable=false and purge anchor series via retention-exclude label; alert for sampling >10% loss of SLO signal.
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic sampler (seeded) and anchor generator math.
Integration test in CI with Otel collector docker-compose that validates labels, sample_rate propagation, and anchor emission.
Load test with k6 simulating 50 tenants (mixed high-card and low-card) to measure cardinality and p95 drift.
Staging canary with synthetic traffic and compare computed SLOs from raw vs anchor series over 48h.
notes:
Trade-offs: Per-tenant sampling reduces ingest but adds complexity in SLA comparisons between tenants with different sample rates. Anchor approach trades some accuracy for cardinality reduction; we must ensure anchors are generated from a deterministic window to avoid introducing bias. Consider future work to store small histograms per tenant instead of anchors for better percentile fidelity.

Open questions: 1) Where to store tenant policies (ConfigMap vs central API) for low-latency evaluation? 2) How to surface sampling opt-in to customers (Console toggle + SDK header)? 3) Whether to expose sample_rate in billing/usage reports.
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created by Ava Chen. Initial problem statement and goals documented.
2025-02-21: Design review with Telemetry and Runtime teams. Agreed to implement Otel processor + remote-write bridge changes. PM requested customer opt-in for sampling.
2025-02-27: PoC of tenant_sampler committed (branch: eng/tenant-sampler-poc). Deterministic sampling verified in unit tests. PR opened: #318.
2025-03-01: Anchor generator prototype showing stable p95 anchors for 50 simulated tenants. Early load test shows 3.6x reduction in active series for high-card dataset.
2025-03-03: Integration test failing intermittently under high concurrency due to reservoir eviction bug; Mate o Ruiz investigating (fix in progress, targeted 2025-03-06).
2025-03-05: Updated ticket with rollout plan and canary criteria after infra sync. Staging canary scheduled for 2025-03-11.
